newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest spot electricity prices mostly steady.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest spot electricity prices mostly steady.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the midwestern U.S. held mostly steady in a day that most power traders characterized as reltively quiet, industry sources said.
Temperatures through much of the Mid-West were expected to be near normal through most of the area through the week.
Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), Wednesday peak, non-firm power prices were discussed steady at $17.00-19.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), the brokers and marketers said.
Off-peak Wednesday non-firm MAPP power was reported to be relatively steady at $11.00-13.00 from $11.00-12.00 on Monday, the sources said.
In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN), peak, non-firm power prices for Wednesday were talked steady at $16.00-18.00, the sources said.
MAIN off peak next day power was also said to be talked steady at $11.00-12.00 per MWh.
Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) for Wednesday were reported to be steady at $15.00-17.00, the sources said.
ECAR electricity prices for off-peak, non-firm delivery were notionally assessed steady at $13.00-15.00 per MWh.
February ECAR was said to have held steady at $22.50-23.00 per MWh, the sources said.

In ECAR, Detroit Edison said Tuesday that its 1,116 megawatt Fermi 2 nuclear power plant will remain shut for at least four more weeks while the company repairs a main generator in the non-nuclear part of the plant.
The unit has been disconnected from the power grid since September 27, when it was shut for scheduled maintenance.
In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP) peak, non-firm power prices for Wednesday delivery were talked steady at $16.00-18.00 through the entire region, the sources said.
Off-peak next day prices throughout SPP were also pegged steady at $12.00-13.00 per MWh.
February SPP was said to have held steady at $22.50-23.00 per MWh.
